question: The radii of two circle are 5 cm and 10 cm and the distance between their centres is 17 cm. Find the length of the transverse common tangent.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of Transverse Common Tangent = √(d² − (R + r)²)

⇒ TCT = √(17² − (10 + 5)²)

⇒ TCT = √(289 − 225)

⇒ TCT = √64 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

**Formula Used:**

The length of the Transverse Common Tangent to two circles is given by:

TCT = √(d² − (R + r)²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ TCT = √(17² − (10 + 5)²)

⇒ TCT = √(17² − 15²)

⇒ TCT = √(289 − 225)

⇒ TCT = √64

⇒ TCT = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The tangent which does not intersect the line segment joining the centres of the circles. Its length is given by: DCT = √(d² − (R − r)²).

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The tangent which intersects the line segment joining the centres. The point of intersection divides the distance between the centres in the ratio of their radii (R : r).

Circles Touching Externally

If two circles touch externally, the distance between centres is d = R + r. The transverse tangent length becomes 0, and the length of the direct common tangent simplifies to 2√(Rr).
